feature: The saved stroke's one click row stays on screen beside a long layers list
summary: On an icon, the Layers pane now starts at a quarter of the panel instead of 40 percent, so with four or five layers and the Styles shelf open the Style row under Line (and its one click Glyph / stroke 1.75 button) is on screen without a scroll in a 1280 by 900 window.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next, no flag changed from its default. Divider over Layers never dragged (or double clicked back).

try.do: File > New > Image, pick Icon, Create, in a window about 900 points tall.
With the Pen draw a two segment line, press Return, pick it with the Select tool (V) and set Width to 1.75 and Corners to Round.
Press Save as Style under Line and press Return to keep the suggested name. The Styles shelf opens at the foot of the panel.
Draw three more Pen lines so Layers counts 5, then pick the last one.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: Press the Glyph / stroke 1.75 button on the Style row without scrolling the panel.
Scroll the Layers list to reach Background and Canvas, or drag the divider under Layers down to show them all.

evaluate: Is four rows of Layers on an icon enough at rest, now that the rest scrolls inside the pane?
Does the cut at the foot of Layers read as a list with more in it, with the count 5 on its header?
Is the Style row where your eye goes when you want the set's stroke?
rough: Only icon documents changed. A picture or a screenshot keeps the 40 percent share, so the same Appearance squeeze still happens there with a path picked and a long list; filed nothing because no report asks for it, noted in the task log.

In a 900 point window the cut under Layers lands exactly between the fourth and fifth row, so no sliver of the fifth row shows; the header count is the only cue there is more. In other window heights the cut falls part way through a row.
Width, Caps and Align under Style are still below the fold with the shelf open; the Style row is the one click that sets them all, so that is the row kept in reach.
Before, for comparison: queue/audits/2026-11-07-saved-stroke-7-width-by-hand-sc.png (four layers, Line the last row in view). After, four layers: 2026-11-12-style-row-four-layers-sc.png.
